correctness.rationale: For reduced p/q and 1<=v<q, nonzero modular residues give the universal floor 1/q. If 0 is present, among 0, lp/q, ..., floor((q-1)/l) lp/q modulo one, two have circular distance at most the reciprocal of their count, at most l/q; their difference is an eligible positive multiple of l. If all nonzero classes are present, either the inverse u of p modulo q is not divisible by l or q-u is not, since l dividing both would contradict gcd(u,q)=1. For necessity choose a missing nonzero t and arbitrarily large q congruent to t modulo l, so gcd(q,l)=1. Take p inverse to l modulo q. If the residue of vp modulo q is a nonzero signed j of magnitude less than q/l, then the representative v is l*j for j>0, or q-l*abs(j) for j<0. These have residues 0 and t respectively, neither allowed. Thus the defining minimum is at least 1/l along infinitely many reduced pairs, ruling out every positive exponent; exponent zero is trivial for nonempty periodic sets once the minimum is defined. The empty-set convention, l=2, periodic counting, and the effect of restoring either class all agree. No unbounded claim is inferred from the finite verifier, which was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The argument classifies complete residue unions of prime period, not general composite-period sets or finite modifications.

value.rationale: This is a complete structural classification on a natural test class for a non-subadditive approximation invariant. It explains why sets of arbitrarily high natural density can have Diophantine density zero even with very regular membership, and why a single restored residue class can change the invariant maximally. Neither a single-class table nor qualitative covering examples supply that boundary.
residual_risks: Value is the complete criterion on prime-periodic sets; effects outside periodic sets or for prescribed composite periods are not claimed.
